reader.requirement: At COBOL-85 with the 1989 Intrinsic Function amendment (as amended in 1993), when FUNCTION MAX has more than one argument every argument (identifier, literal, arithmetic expression, function, table ALL reference) must be of one class of the three 1985 classes (numeric, alphanumeric, alphabetic), with alphabetic and alphanumeric arguments allowed to mix; numeric-edited and group items count as class alphanumeric (§1985:IV.4.3.3) and a numeric argument beside an alphanumeric or alphabetic one is refused.

edition-consulted.switches: sig.IntroducedIn > ctx.Edition.DialectLevel: MAX's catalog row has IntroducedIn 85, so the function is available at --std 85
ArgPredicate.AppliesAt(edition year) for MAX's tail predicate NotStrongGroup (Since 85, unreachable at 1985 which has no TYPE clause); the cross-class rule itself is asked unconditionally

reader.edition-search: Read CheckArgumentClasses, the MAX row of IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified (Uniform 'p' + CrossArgRule.AllSameClass), CrossViolation, CrossBlock and the class readers ClassOf1/ClassOfPlace/ClassOfItem/ClassOfPic; grep for DialectLevel / Edition in IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs finds none on the class or cross path.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no for this rule: the same intersection screen runs at every edition; later editions add classes (national, boolean, index arguments) that a 1985 program cannot declare.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f33_02 exercises the rule's legal mixing; the refusal of numeric with alphanumeric/alphabetic/numeric-edited/ref-modified/function arguments and the group-as-alphanumeric reading are not exercised.

probes.printed: A/X ABD; A/LIT ABC; NE/X ABD; G/X ZZ; N +0007.00; EXPR +0014.00; ALL +0009.00; RM/X 6; FN/X abc; FN/N +0007.00; ONE +0007.00
probes.expected: legal: alphabetic with alphanumeric item and literal, numeric-edited and group (class alphanumeric) with alphanumeric, numeric items/literals/expressions/table ALL/integer function, ref-modified numeric (class alphanumeric) with alphanumeric literal, alphanumeric function with literal; values are the maximum per A.2.23.4

probes.printed: error COBOL1627: FUNCTION MAX argument-2 is of class alphanumeric, which cannot agree with the earlier arguments (MAX(1 "A"))
error COBOL1627: argument-2 is of class alphanumeric (MAX(numeric, numeric-edited))
probes.expected: refused: numeric-edited is class alphanumeric at 1985

probes.printed: error COBOL1627: argument-2 is of class numeric (MAX(alphabetic, numeric))
probes.expected: refused: the exception is alphabetic with alphanumeric only

probes.printed: error COBOL1627: argument-3 is of class numeric (MAX(WX WA WN2))
error COBOL1627: argument-2 is of class alphanumeric (MAX(WN2 WN2(1:2)))
probes.expected: refused: a reference-modified item is class alphanumeric

probes.printed: error COBOL1627: argument-2 is of class numeric (MAX(CURRENT-DATE WN2))
error COBOL1627: argument-2 is of class numeric (MAX(WX WN2 + 1))
probes.expected: refused: an arithmetic expression is numeric

probes.printed: error COBOL6979: the index data item 'WIX' is an intrinsic function argument (ISO §1985:VI.5.14.3 SR5)
probes.expected: refused at 1985 (an index data item may not be an argument)
no AR1 violation: ZERO takes the numeric class beside a numeric argument

citations.check: OK  §1989:A.2.23.3 AR1  (2.23.3 Arguments)  the text is in AR1
OK  §1985:IV.4.3.3  (4.3.3 Concept of Classes of Data)  the text is in the clause

reader.notes: Conforms. The cross screen projects numeric-edited to class alphanumeric and merges alphabetic with alphanumeric, which matches §1985:IV.4.3.3's three classes plus the 1993 exception. Message text at --std 85 cites §2023:15.59.3 r2 rather than the 1989 rule. Whether a figurative constant is an admissible MAX argument at all is A.1's question, not this rule's.

refuter.evidence: m1legal.cob at --std 85, EXIT 0: MAX(alphabetic, numeric-edited) 'ABC'; MAX(alphabetic, group) 'ABC'; MAX(alphanumeric-edited PIC XBX, alphabetic, literal) 'ZZ'; MAX(alphanumeric table ALL, alphabetic) 'CC'; MAX(P-scaled, COMP signed, SIGN LEADING SEPARATE) +0300.00; MAX(LENGTH function, numeric) +0003.00; MAX(CHAR function, alphabetic) 'ABC' (all values the maximum by A.2.23.4). Refused COBOL1627: m2aenum.cob MAX(alphanumeric-edited, numeric); m3tabnum.cob MAX(numeric, alphanumeric-table ALL); m4chrnum.cob MAX(numeric, CHAR function). m5nat.cob MAX(WX, N"AB") refused (COBOL0900 national literal requires COBOL-2002, plus COBOL1627). cite.py: 'OK  §1989:A.2.23.3 AR1  (2.23.3 Arguments)  the text is in AR1'.
